newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures rise, continued asset allocation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures rise, continued asset allocation.

text.p: U.S. debt futures rose early on continued asset allocation into T-bonds and out of stocks after revisions to U.S. first-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) were out of the way, traders said.
"GDP is old news," one bond futures market analyst said. "You do know that all of this (bond rally) is asset allocation out of stocks."

Floor traders and analysts said the asset allocation started late Thursday on growing expectations that Intel Corp would announce lower-than-expected second quarter results. Intel made the announcement early Friday morning.
Intel said revenue and net income for its fiscal second quarter will fall below expectations due to weaker-than-projected demand, particularly in Europe.
Several analysts said the forecasts from Intel, a bellwether stock in the technology sector, would lead to a sell-off in the stock of computer-related companies.
They said funds and portfolio managers were putting profits from those stocks into U.S. T-bonds and notes.
September T-bonds, which became lead contract month in Thursday's night session, rallied to 109-12/32, through the 100-day moving average at 109-07/32.

September T-bonds ticked up to 109-06/32 after preliminary GDP estimates were released. U.S. first-quarter GDP was revised to show a gain of 5.8 percent, versus estimates for up 6.0 percent and against the advance estimate of 5.6 percent.
"It helped the market briefly," one Eurodollar futures trader said, noting that the implicit deflator was downwardly revised to up 2.2 percent, from advance estimates of up 2.3 percent.
However, asset allocation into bonds was the primary factor that propelled December Eurodollars to their highest level of the week at 93.74.
Further resistance is at the May 23 high of 93.75.
"If I knew where the heck resistance was (in bonds), I'd sell it," one market trader said.
Most traders are pegging September bond's next resistance levels at 109-20/32 and at the 200-day moving average at 109-23/32.
However, traders are still awaiting the U.S. April new home sales data and the May Chicago National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.
"Probably the most important data today is the May Chicago NAPM," one analyst said.
"This data is significant in that it is current," he said.
Chicago NAPM for May is seen on average falling to 56.8 from 57.2 in April. New home sales are seen at an annual rate of 800,000 units versus 813,000 in March.
The final May University of Michigan sentiment survey will also be released at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT. Sentiment is expected to rise to 104.0.

At 0830 CDT/1330 GMT, September T-bonds were up 14/32 at 109-12/32, 10-year notes were up 05/32 at 106-21/32, December Eurodollars were up 0.035 at 93.735 and March Eurodollars were 0.045 higher at 93.61. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
